pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: I run your tool as `tool | jq .` and as `tool > out.txt`. What goes to stdout, what goes to stderr, and how do you decide which is which?
expected_points: stdout carries the data the user asked for — what flows down a pipeline
stderr carries diagnostics: progress, prompts, warnings, verbose logs
the test is 'would a script parse this?', not 'is it bad news?'
progress or prompts on stdout corrupt piped data; results on stderr starve the pipeline
the exit code is the third channel

questions.prompt: How does your program know whether it is talking to a terminal, and what changes when it isn't? Where in the program does that question get asked?
expected_points: stat the file and test os.ModeCharDevice, or golang.org/x/term.IsTerminal for the accurate answer
caveat: /dev/null is a character device too; Windows consoles need extra setup
when it isn't a terminal: no colour, no cursor redraws, no prompting — the information survives, the decoration doesn't
detection happens once at the edge and is passed down as a bool, which is what makes everything below testable
stdin, stdout and stderr can each be redirected independently

questions.prompt: State your colour decision chain from the top. What does NO_COLOR do, and what happens when NO_COLOR=1 and --color=always are both present?
expected_points: an ordered, written-down chain: never / always / NO_COLOR / TERM=dumb / is-a-terminal
NO_COLOR is a cross-tool convention: set and non-empty means no colour, whatever the value
NO_COLOR set to the empty string is not a veto
the explicit per-invocation flag beats the environment default here — and the learner can defend that ordering
the chain is a pure function of (mode, isTerminal, env), so it is testable without a terminal

--no-color is a shorthand folding into the same chain as --color=never, not a second mechanism: users expect the boolean, the three-valued --color is what makes 'auto' expressible, and both must land on one decision function

questions.prompt: Describe what your progress indicator writes on a terminal and what it writes when stderr is a CI log file. Why that stream, and why is it driven by Update calls rather than a timer?
expected_points: on a terminal: \r, the status, and \x1b[K to erase the tail of a longer previous line, redrawn in place
off a terminal: nothing during the run, one plain summary line at the end — no \r, no escapes
it goes to stderr so redirected or piped stdout stays clean data
explicit updates keep the output deterministic and testable; a timer means a goroutine, wall-clock flakiness, and races
real tools throttle redraws, but that belongs outside the tested piece

questions.prompt: Walk me through your Ask: the default, validation, and what happens in a CI job with no terminal and no default.
expected_points: the default is shown in brackets and an empty answer takes it
validation rejects with a message and re-asks, with a cap so the loop terminates
with no terminal it never reads or writes: the default, or ErrNotInteractive naming what to pass instead
a tool that blocks on a prompt in a pipeline or CI is broken; --yes exists for this
one bufio.Scanner for the session — a fresh one per question eats buffered input

questions.prompt: What does a TUI framework like Bubble Tea give you that line-based output doesn't, and when is it the wrong answer?
expected_points: the Elm-style loop: a model, Update(msg) returning a new model plus commands, View rendering the whole screen
the framework owns the event loop, alternate screen, raw input and repainting
right for long-lived interactive sessions the user stays inside
wrong for run-do-work-report tools: not pipeable, greppable or scriptable, awkward in CI, over ssh, in dumb terminals and for screen readers
and markedly harder to test than a function writing to an io.Writer

questions.prompt: You want to realign the human output columns and rename a JSON field. Which one can you do in a patch release, and why?
expected_points: the human format is not an API; the machine format is
JSON shape changes like an API changes — other people's scripts depend on it
JSON on stdout alone, diagnostics on stderr, never styled
emit a document like {"results": …} rather than a bare array so it can grow fields
encode an empty slice, not a nil one, so consumers never meet null

questions.prompt: Why does `fmt.Sprintf("%-4s", painted)` break your columns when colour is on, and what did you do instead?
expected_points: %-4s pads to the length of the string it is given, and the escape characters count toward that length even though they occupy no columns
coloured lines end up shorter on screen than plain ones
pad by the visible status word, then paint — or paint and pad separately
